summary: Port reproduces the pattern's architecture exactly — a deterministic 6-segment cycle of shimmer looks joined by per-pixel dissolves, with the rotating-bar look pixel-identical — but it runs 1.2x slow overall (2.4x slow inside the bar look), replaces the original's fire/red-orange palette with a cyan-blue-magenta one, and draws the radial-glow look as a ~3x3 lattice of small dim blobs where the original draws one canvas-filling glow.
observations: Both sides are 16x16 grid, no controls, no sensors, and are FULLY DETERMINISTIC: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 render identical stats on both sides, and both are time-based (bar angle at t=1s is 73-75 deg on orig and 32-34 deg on port at 10, 20 AND 40 fps — no frame-rate coupling on either side).

CYCLE LENGTH: original repeats byte-identically every 30.000 s (dump t=1 vs t=31 vs t=61 -> meanAbsDiff 0.00); port repeats every 36.000 s (t=1 vs t=37 vs t=73 -> 0.00). Port cycle is 1.20x too long. Neither drifts over a 240 s window.

ARCHITECTURE MATCHES: each cycle is 6 equal segments (orig 5 s each, port 6 s each) crossfaded by a per-pixel random dissolve. The segment TYPES correspond one-for-one on both sides: [rotating white bar, soft radial-glow field, hard-edged 'voronoi cell' field, rotating white bar, radial-glow field, cell field], and both cycles end on the same grey-horizontal-band frame before the next bar segment.

BAR SEGMENT IS PIXEL-PERFECT BUT 2.4x SLOW. A time-rescale scan (--fps 100, whole-frame meanAbsDiff over 0-255) gives: orig@t=1.00s vs port@t=2.40s -> 0.99; k=2.30 -> 7.76, k=2.50 -> 6.07, k=2.60 -> 12.34; while orig@1.00 vs port@1.00 -> 52.39. Best k = 2.40 exactly. Confirmed by orientation tracking (2nd-moment fit on pixels >40): orig sweeps 4 deg -> 180 deg in 2.45 s (~72 deg/s, a full 180 deg turn every 2.5 s, i.e. 2 half-turns per 5 s segment); port sweeps 1 deg -> 148 deg in 5.0 s (~29.5 deg/s, one half-turn per 6 s segment).

The bar's SHAPE is identical: at t=0 the column-24 vertical profile on a 48x48 grid is character-for-character the same on both sides ('.................++##########++.................') — a single 10 px-wide band with 2 px soft shoulders.

PALETTE (biggest divergence). 80 frames sampled across 240 s, hue histogram of coloured pixels (saturation >= 0.15, value >= 12), 30 deg bins: ORIG 0deg:41% 30deg:10% 60deg:4% 90deg:4% 120deg:4% 150deg:7% 180deg:8% 210deg:5% 240deg:5% 270deg:5% 300deg:4% 330deg:5% (51% of all colour in 0-60 deg = red/orange). PORT 0deg:4.5% 30deg:2% 60deg:2% 90deg:2% 120deg:1% 150deg:10% 180deg:21% 210deg:16% 240deg:11% 270deg:11% 300deg:10% 330deg:9% (59% in 150-270 deg = cyan/azure/blue). Grey fraction and saturation DO match (orig 23.9% grey / mean sat 0.76; port 24.6% / 0.75), so the white-bar segments are fine — the divergence is entirely in the coloured looks.

PER-SEGMENT COLOUR: the original's two CELL segments are effectively MONOCHROME FIRE — 91% and 92% of their coloured pixels fall in hue 0-30 deg, the rest in 30-60 deg (a dark-red -> orange -> yellow-orange ramp on black). The port's corresponding segments are full-spectrum (top bins 180deg:19%/210deg:12%/300deg:12% and 300deg:18%/0deg:12%/180deg:11%) — cyan/blue/magenta gradient-filled cells.

PER-SEGMENT COLOUR (glow segments): the original's radial-glow segments span the WHOLE wheel with warm peaks (seg1 0deg:15% 180deg:19% 150deg:11%; seg4 0deg:14% 150deg:17% 120deg:10%) — visually a green/cyan core ringed by yellow, orange, red, purple. The port's glow segments have essentially NO warm content (seg1 0-120 deg totals 7%; seg4 0-120 deg totals 0%) and sit entirely in 150-360 deg — dark-red/maroon cores with magenta rims.

GLOW-FIELD SPATIAL FREQUENCY ~3x TOO HIGH. On a 48x48 grid, row-wise circular autocorrelation of the brightness field finds NO repeat within the canvas for the original at t=5.5/6.5/22.5/23.5/25.5/26.5/27.5 s (one feature spanning the whole canvas), while the port shows a clear repeat at lag 14-20 px at t=5.5/6.5/8.5/21.5/22.5/28.5 s — i.e. 2.4-3.4 blobs across the canvas. Visually: original = one big soft glow; port = a 5x5 -> 4x4 -> 3x3 -> 2x2 lattice of small blobs.
The port's glow segment also covers more of the rig: 143 and 147 lit pixels/frame out of 256 (56-57%) vs the original's 95 and 134 (37% and 52%).

BRIGHTNESS ENVELOPE: the original's 5th segment ramps to a FULL-CANVAS SATURATED rainbow glow — frame-mean V hits 255 at t=23.5 s, and whole-frame meanBrightness peaks at 134 over the 240 s survey. The port never gets near that: its best frame-mean V in the corresponding segment is 125 and its 240 s meanBrightness max is 70. Segment-average brightness otherwise tracks well (bar 38/35 orig vs 34/35 port; cells 103/100 vs 86/98).

DISSOLVE RATE: both crossfade with a per-pixel random dissolve out of a short black gap. Measuring lit-pixel count (max channel > 15, of 256) at 0.1 s steps: original ramps 0 -> 130 between t=8.4 s and t=9.7 s (~1.3 s, 26% of its 5 s segment); port ramps 9 -> 128 between t=12.2 s and t=12.7 s (~0.5 s, 8% of its 6 s segment). Port's dissolve is noticeably snappier both absolutely and proportionally.

CELL-FIELD GEOMETRY is similar but not identical: best mask IoU between orig@11.0 s and a scan of port times is 0.54 (at port@12.6 s), with lit counts 94 vs 117-130 — the port lights ~30% more of the grid in that look. No time-rescale factor aligns the cell segments the way k=2.40 aligns the bar segments (best meanAbsDiff across k=0..4.2 was 44, vs 0.99 for the bar).

RESOLUTION INDEPENDENCE MATCHES: re-rendered at 8x8, 16x16 and 48x48, both sides draw the same picture at finer/coarser detail (feature counts and sizes unchanged) — neither rasterizes at native resolution.
CONTROL SURFACE MATCHES: --probe-controls reports '(no settable controls)' for BOTH sides; meta.json lists an empty controls array on each. No missing/extra/renamed dials.
Neither side binds sensor globals (wantsSensors false on both), so the beat120 feed is a no-op here.

Motion stats over the 240 s survey: orig motion avg 46, meanBrightness avg 39, trend steady, 6 zero-motion frames of 480; port motion avg 40, meanBrightness avg 34, trend steady, 1 zero-motion frame. Neither side dies, freezes or decays — the port's steady state is its 36 s cycle repeating cleanly.
feedback: Cycle timing: the port's segment duration is 6 s where the original's is 5 s, making the whole cycle 36 s instead of 30 s. Shorten the per-look hold by 1/6 so the full loop repeats every 30.000 s (verifiable: frame at t and t+30 must be byte-identical).

Rotating-bar look: the bar's shape and rendering are ALREADY EXACT (identical 10 px profile), only its rate is wrong — it rotates at ~30 deg/s and should rotate at ~72 deg/s, i.e. a full 180 deg turn every 2.5 s so the bar makes TWO half-turns per segment instead of one. The measured rescale factor is exactly 2.40 (orig@t == port@2.40*t to within 1/255 mean pixel error), so multiply the bar look's angular rate by 2.4 (equivalently: after fixing the 1.2x segment-length error, still double it).

Palette is the headline visual gap. The original's 'cell/voronoi' look is a near-monochrome FIRE ramp — 91-92% of its coloured pixels sit in hue 0-30 deg (dark red -> orange -> yellow-orange on black); the port renders those same cells in full-spectrum cyan/blue/magenta. Constrain that look's hue to roughly 0-0.17 of the wheel.

The original's radial-glow look uses a WIDE rainbow radial ramp with a warm bias (green/cyan core -> yellow -> orange -> red -> purple rim; hue bins 0deg:15%, 150deg:11%, 180deg:19%). The port's glow is confined to hue 150-360 deg with essentially zero red/orange/yellow/green (0-120 deg totals 0-7%). Restore the warm half of the ramp.

Overall: the original spends 51% of its coloured pixels in hue 0-60 deg; the port spends 8%. Whatever hue term drives the coloured looks appears to be offset/rotated toward cyan — check for a ~+0.5 hue offset or a swapped R/B channel in the palette lookup.

Radial-glow spatial frequency is ~3x too high: at 48x48 the port's glow field repeats every 14-20 px (2.5-3.5 blobs across the canvas) while the original has no repeat within the canvas at all (one glow spanning the whole rig). Divide that look's spatial scale by ~3 so a single blob fills the frame.

The original's 5th segment climaxes in a full-canvas SATURATED glow (frame-mean value reaches 255); the port's equivalent peaks at 125 and stays a dim lattice. Whatever drives that brightness ramp is capped or diluted in the port.
Crossfade dissolve is too fast: the original's per-pixel dissolve ramps lit pixels 0 -> 130/256 over ~1.3 s; the port does it in ~0.5 s. Stretch the dissolve to ~1.3 s (about a quarter of a segment).

Things already right and worth not breaking: exact determinism and seed-independence, fps-invariance (time-based, not frame-stepped), the 6-segment look sequence and its ordering, resolution independence across 8x8/16x16/48x48, the empty control surface, the white/grey balance (24% grey pixels, mean saturation 0.75), and the bar look's pixel geometry.
